description: Width tiers for Dance — Years 9-10 band
subject: Dance

width_notes.minimum_width: The narrowest honest floor for the descriptor's command term at senior level. For Y9-10 Dance, minimum requires demonstrable genre/style technique, motif development, contextual analysis, or reflective documentation — not just participation.
width_notes.typical_width: Full descriptor scope from elaborations — covers motif manipulation, genre/style proficiency, contextual investigation, identity-driven reflection and collaborative practice as intended for this band.
width_notes.wider: Enrichment adding genre/style contexts, cultural investigations, professional practice research, or extended reflective and portfolio work. First Nations Australian content in wider throughout.
width_notes.elaborations: ACARA elaborations used as source data. Y9-10 elaborations foreground motif manipulation, musculoskeletal safety, First Nations identity and challenge, and sustained reflective documentation.

AC9ADA10C01.minimum_width: Develop a movement motif; apply at least two manipulation techniques to generate material; structure a dance communicating a clear idea, perspective or meaning with at least one choreographic form.
AC9ADA10C01.typical_width: Choreograph dance communicating ideas about identity, belonging or social justice; develop motifs and manipulate elements (addition, diminution, force, tempo, body parts); use Viewpoints to interrogate spatial and dynamic choices; use style-specific forms; adapt influences from different cultural sources respectfully; document process.
wider: Develop motifs that synthesise influences from dances of multiple cultures, times and places — using respectful adaptation to create original work that expresses a personal perspective
Use social media movement trends or viral dances as starting points — manipulating these into original work that challenges or recontextualises the source material
Create a dance that takes a specific political or social justice position — using structural and device choices as argumentative tools
elaborations: experimenting with ways to combine choreographic devices such as addition and diminution, force and tempo
using Viewpoints relating to forms and elements when choreographing about identity, belonging or social justice
adapting dance ideas from different cultural influences respectfully
developing movement motifs and using devices innovatively to communicate choreographic intent
using motifs from known dances on social media as starting points for extension
using style-specific forms to structure a dance

AC9ADA10C02.minimum_width: Identify and demonstrate at least three characteristic techniques of a selected genre/style; apply musculoskeletal knowledge to safe execution; use one Viewpoints-based feedback cycle to refine.
AC9ADA10C02.typical_width: Apply knowledge of musculoskeletal system to safe technique execution; build and apply genre/style-specific techniques through sustained observation and practice; seek feedback using Viewpoints questions and refine technical and expressive skill application; develop proficiency over time.
wider: Study a genre or style associated with a culture students identify with — using community knowledge and resources to inform authentic technique application
Analyse a physically demanding technique through an anatomical lens — identifying injury risks, safe modification strategies, and professional practice approaches to injury prevention
Compare how the same movement vocabulary functions in two related genre/styles — developing nuanced stylistic literacy
elaborations: applying knowledge of the structure and function of the musculoskeletal system to execute movements safely
using observations of a dance in a selected genre/style to identify and build characteristic techniques over time
seeking feedback using Viewpoints to refine technical and expressive skills

AC9ADA10D01.minimum_width: Set a specific technical skill development goal; demonstrate improvement in at least one technical quality; demonstrate proficiency in at least two genre/style-specific techniques.
AC9ADA10D01.typical_width: Refine technical skills through self-reflection: control, accuracy, strength, balance, alignment, flexibility, endurance, coordination, articulation; use improvisation and experimentation to develop expressive technique across genres/styles; practise and refine genre/style-specific technique toward proficiency; apply safe dance practice as demands increase.
wider: Develop a sustained personal technical development plan across two or three skills over an extended period — setting measurable targets and documenting progress
Pursue technique development in a genre or style associated with a cultural identity or tradition — engaging with community knowledge where appropriate
Research how professional dance practitioners in a chosen style approach technical training, injury prevention and recovery — applying this knowledge to personal practice
elaborations: refining technical skills in response to self-reflection to develop safe dance practice and control, accuracy, strength, balance, alignment, flexibility, endurance, coordination, articulation
using experimentation and improvisation to develop techniques for expressive skills in a range of genres/styles
practising and refining technical skills to develop proficiency in genre- and style-specific techniques

AC9ADA10D02.minimum_width: Use at least two Viewpoints questions to analyse element or device use in own or another's work; connect analysis to one choreographic or performance decision; identify one personal influence shaping choreographic choices.
AC9ADA10D02.typical_width: Reflect on element and device use using Viewpoints; evaluate choreographic and performance choices; document creative process including analysis and evaluation; improvise and analyse movement choices to reflect individuality; consider how emotion, political positions, critical theories and lived experiences influence approach to dance.
wider: Maintain a systematic reflective journal across an extended choreographic project — analysing key decision points, pivots, and the relationship between intent and realised work
Investigate a choreographer whose political or social identity is central to their practice — analysing how personal position translates into specific choreographic choices
Analyse a professional dance work for element and device use — applying the same analytical framework to evaluate own choreographic process
elaborations: using Viewpoints to reflect on and evaluate use of forms and elements
evaluating choreographic and performance choices
documenting creative process including analysis and evaluation in reflective records
improvising using elements and analysing movement choices to reflect individuality
considering how emotion, political statements, critical theories or experiences influence and shape approach to dance

AC9ADA10E01.minimum_width: Investigate one choreographer or performer — connecting their cultural, social or historical context to at least two identifiable choices in their work.
AC9ADA10E01.typical_width: Investigate how and why choreographers and performers work with communities to advocate for social justice or sustainable living; explore specific practitioners working with communities in Australia and Asia; analyse how traditions, styles and contexts affect interpretation; extend movement vocabulary by analysing styles from cultures students identify with; use Viewpoints to interrogate choreographic intent.
wider: Investigate a choreographer whose practice is grounded in a specific cultural community — analysing how community context shapes choreographic decisions at every level
Compare how two choreographers from different cultural or historical contexts address the same theme — analysing how context determines approach, structural form and reception
Investigate how a dance style from a country or region in Asia has been adopted, adapted or appropriated in Western contexts — using analysis to inform respectful practice
elaborations: investigating how and why choreographers work collaboratively with communities in Australia with cultural links to Asia
investigating how and why choreographers work with communities to advocate for sustainability and social justice
investigating why different traditions, styles and contexts affect experience and interpretation
extending movement vocabulary through exploration of stylistic preferences and analysis of styles from different times and cultures
analysing element use in popular culture styles or styles from Asia as stimulus for choreography

AC9ADA10E02.minimum_width: Describe how one First Nations Australian dance work either celebrates or challenges a perspective of Australian identity — connecting at least two choreographic choices to the practitioner's position.
AC9ADA10E02.typical_width: Evaluate how First Nations Australian choreographers and performers work with communities to explore local histories, cultures and identities; investigate dance works that challenge understandings of 'first contacts'; explore how practitioners communicate lived experiences to broader communities.
wider: Investigate a First Nations Australian choreographer's sustained practice — examining how their work has evolved in response to historical and contemporary political events
Compare how two different First Nations Australian dance practitioners address Australian identity — analysing how different community positions produce different choreographic choices
Investigate how a specific First Nations Australian dance work was received by different audiences — examining how community and non-community audiences read the same work differently
elaborations: evaluating ways First Nations Australian performers and choreographers work respectfully with communities to explore local histories and identities
investigating dance works that challenge understandings about 'first contacts' between First Nations Peoples and colonisers
exploring ways First Nations Australian choreographers use their practice to communicate ideas, messages and lived experiences to the broader community

AC9ADA10P01.minimum_width: Perform in a selected genre/style with at least two style-specific techniques; execute entry and exit consistent with genre/style; use at least one production element purposefully.
AC9ADA10P01.typical_width: Rehearse and perform dance for audiences using technical and expressive skills and genre/style-specific techniques; plan entry/exit consistent with genre/mood; build spatial placement confidence through rehearsal; use production elements to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives or meaning.
wider: Perform in a culturally specific genre/style with input or guidance from community representatives — developing authentic engagement beyond surface imitation
Choreograph entry and exit as deliberate compositional elements — using them to establish and resolve the performance's communicative arc
Perform in more than one genre/style context during the year — comparing performance demands, audience relationships, and the different communicative capacities each context creates
elaborations: planning how to enter and leave the performance space consistently with genre/style, mood or ideas conveyed
using rehearsal to build confidence in accurate and fluent spatial placement maintenance
using available production elements to enhance communication of ideas, perspectives or meaning
